title: How Your EV Turns DC Into AC: The Inverter ⚡🔁 #shorts

scenes.text: Your EV's battery speaks one language, and its motor speaks another. Something has to translate.
The battery stores direct current, flowing one way. Most EV motors run on three-phase alternating current: three waves, each a third of a cycle apart.
The translator is the inverter: six power switches, arranged in three pairs.
They flick on and off up to twenty thousand times a second. The motor's coils smooth those pulses into clean waves.
Raise the wave's frequency, and the motor spins faster. Push more current, and you get more torque.
When you slow down, it works in reverse, turning the motor's AC back into DC for the battery.
So your accelerator pedal is really a request to a chip. Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
